answer: Sybil herds die at a handshake gate with a price floor: every new agent identity must solve a per-epoch nonce chained to its own paid registration, and the difficulty target ratchets up with signup volume, so a farm of clones burns real compute and cash per seat, and entry becomes as scarce as saffron, every clone's pigment costing more than the last. Reputation then scales with capital at risk, so a young delta of clones carries almost no weight. An attacker's cost grows linearly with identities while influence stays flat.
